title: Bound loss with a private matching before composing a memory guard
statement: For private uniform perfect matching n=2m>=4 and the same arbitrary CPTP/leakage operation, singlet loss with a K-dimensional reset-completed code obeys Bell loss<=C q, C=(d/K)(n+2)/(n-1). Exact partial-swap constructions give the full-code sharp coefficient. The operator-valued guard can use this bound only at the same service boundary.

requires: Private uniform matching on n=2m>=4 and one role-independent complete CPTP operation on the same boundary
Actual code dimension K, singlet input dimension d and complete reset/leakage decoder
Retain current quantum memory and purification and all accepted-record dependence
provides: For private uniform perfect matching n=2m>=4 and the same arbitrary CPTP/leakage operation, singlet loss with a K-dimensional reset-completed code obeys Bell loss<=C q, C=(d/K)(n+2)/(n-1). assumptions: Current roles/settings/pads must be private and source boundaries/timing/ports identical for test and service. Full logical tests pay encoder/decoder; probe-only tests need a separate budget for them. V9 is conditional on one completed learning history and disclosed source-rule boundary; no training-average yield, same-time/gate winner, native hardware or superiority. Later matching comparison is separately scoped.
costs: Direct pair routing O(n); nearest-neighbor line routing quadratic
All calibration, learning, buffers, controls, source calls and actual encoder/decoder operations; conventional 2MUB/Pauli comparators use the same learned code
